intro: Two kinds come up: sizing something ("how many X") and explaining a change ("metric Y dropped, why"). Interviewers score the structure and the assumptions, not the final number.

sizing.title: Sizing something
steps: Pick a path: top-down (start from a big population, narrow it) or bottom-up (start from one unit, multiply up).
State the population you start from, out loud, with a number.
Apply one filter at a time. Say the assumption before each: penetration, frequency, price.
Multiply through. Round hard — keep the arithmetic simple.
Sanity check against something you know. If it's 10x off a real figure, find which assumption is wrong.

example.q: How many cups of chai are sold in Mumbai per day?
work: ~5k tea stalls in Mumbai × ~2k cups = 10M. Close enough.

diagnosis.title: RCA — a metric dropped, explain it
diagnosis.note: The most common PM interview format there is: "Orders dropped 20% this week. Do a root cause analysis." Don't guess a cause — narrow it down with a method.
steps: Confirm it's real. Is the drop bigger than normal week-to-week noise? Is the tracking still working?
Segment. Platform, region, new vs existing, free vs paid. Everywhere, or one slice?
Time it. When exactly did it start? Line that up against releases, experiments, campaigns, outages.
Split the metric. Watch time = users × sessions × minutes per session. Which factor moved?
Check the outside world. Competitor launch, a holiday, a news event, seasonality.
Form one hypothesis, test it cheaply, then decide.

mece.note: Once you're narrowing causes, sort them into four buckets so you cover everything without overlap — MECE: mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive.

buckets.label: System
buckets.examples: Tracking broke, a metric definition changed, a dashboard bug

buckets.label: Internal
buckets.examples: A release, a pricing change, a bug, a design change, an outage on our side

buckets.label: External
buckets.examples: A competitor's promotion, a payment provider outage, a market shift

buckets.label: Out of control
buckets.examples: A holiday, weather, a regional event, a natural disaster

questionSets.note: No product involved. Practise the population funnel.

questions.q: How many people in India use public transport daily?
questions.check: Indian Railways alone carries 20M+ a day, and city buses carry several times that. Fits.

questions.q: How many school teachers are there in India?
questions.check: Govt schools run fuller classes, private ones smaller. Averaging to 30 is fair.

questions.q: How many litres of milk are consumed in Bengaluru per day?
questions.check: Per person that is ~0.25 L, about a cup and a bit. Believable for tea, coffee, curd and cooking.

questions.q: How many weddings happen in India each year?
steps: ~25M, so ~25M people turn marriageable each year
questions.check: The wedding industry usually quotes ~10M. Same ballpark.

questions.q: How many mobile phone screens crack in Delhi each month?
questions.check: Supply check: ~2,000 repair shops × ~4 screens a day × 30 days = ~240k. Both routes agree.

questionSets.note: Physical goods and services. Watch replacement rate and seasonality.

questions.q: How many cars are sold in Pune in a year?
questions.check: India sells ~4M cars a year. Pune is ~0.5% of people but richer, so ~1.5% share → ~60k.

questions.q: How many umbrellas are sold in Mumbai during monsoon?
questions.check: At ~₹250 each that is ~₹100 crore. Sensible for one city's seasonal product.

questions.q: How many pizzas does Domino's sell in India per day?
questions.check: 480k × 365 × ~₹300 ≈ ₹5,000 crore a year. Same order of magnitude as its reported revenue.

questions.q: How many ACs are installed in Chennai each summer?
questions.check: India sells ~9M ACs a year. Chennai is ~1% of people but hotter and richer, so ~1.2% → ~100k.

questions.q: How many cricket bats are sold in India per year?
questions.check: Mostly cheap tennis-ball bats. At ~₹300 that is ~₹150 crore, a plausible niche market.

questionSets.note: Digital. Chain population → internet → smartphone → app → active use.

questions.q: How many WhatsApp messages are sent in India per day?
questions.check: WhatsApp has publicly said it carries ~100B a day worldwide. India at ~15% of that fits.

questions.q: How many food-delivery orders does Swiggy get in a tier-2 city per day?
steps: ~4 a month → ~240k a month, ~8k a day
questions.check: Metros do most of the volume. A tier-2 city landing in the low thousands is reasonable.

questions.q: How much storage would Google Photos need for all of India?
steps: ~1,000 a year × ~3 MB = ~3 GB a year
questions.check: 15 GB is the free quota, so most users sit near it. That matches.

questions.q: How many UPI transactions happen in India per day?
questions.check: Check against NPCI's published monthly volume. Volume keeps growing, so use the latest figure.

questions.q: How many hours of video does an average Indian Instagram user watch per week?
questions.check: The ~30 min a day matches commonly reported averages. The 60% video share is the assumption to defend.

questions.q: How many rides does Rapido complete in Hyderabad per day?
questions.check: Two independent routes landing within 1.5×. That is the point of the check.

anchors.title: Numbers to memorise
anchors.note: Round, current-ish figures. Good enough for a guesstimate — state them as assumptions.
